mintAuthority.summary: USDKG is issued natively on Ethereum and Tron through immutable Tether-style contracts whose issue() and redeem() functions are owner-gated. Each deployment is controlled by a separate verified 3-of-7 multisig: 0xcF355a...7377 on Ethereum and TEmt2R...A8jd on Tron.

controls.label: Gold Dollar issuance backend
controls.evidence: Gold Dollar operates the centralized 1:1 mint/redeem for USDKG against custodied physical gold, with KYC/AML required for all redemptions; no permissionless or user-collateralized mint route exists.

controls.label: USDKG Ethereum token owner (3-of-7 multisig)
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 26095805, owner() on USDKG token 0xe820c06321e60d36257c666643fa5436643445e3 returned 0xcf355ad32abf378f067fa93a28d96a767feb7377. getOwners() returned seven owners and getThreshold() returned 3. The implementation, admin, and beacon EIP-1967 slots were zero. The ConsenSys Diligence audit describes the custom multisig with upgradeability and owner/threshold modification removed, and owner-gated issue()/redeem(). Zero proxy slots alone do not establish immutability.

controls.label: USDKG Tron token owner (3-of-7 multisig)
controls.evidence: At Tron block 84453790, owner() on TXZo12...nwEG returned 0x34b436...4fd5, the Tron address TEmt2R...A8jd. The verified owner contract ABI and current constant calls returned seven owners (TVZwUL...Jao, TQHTXd...XLU, TXAjos...WDG, TSfP1D...8vB, TZ5KnE...aXL, TMy7WS...bKw, and TEPMSb...AZv) and getThreshold() = 3. The custom multisig has no owner-management, module, or guard functions, and the token's issue() and redeem() functions are owner-gated.

review.evidence: Gold Dollar operates native owner-gated issue/redeem contracts on Ethereum and Tron. Historical control reviews identified separate 3-of-7 multisigs; the Ethereum owner and quorum were re-confirmed at block 26095805 on 2026-10-01. The transparency portal indexes one reserve report, the November 2025 Kreston ISRS 4400 agreed-upon-procedures report; the January 2025 ConsenSys document is a smart-contract audit, not a second reserve snapshot. Kreston's report observes gold held on 2025-11-28 and states that no tokens had yet been put in circulation at the report date. The report expresses no opinion or assurance and does not prove a recurring series of liability reconciliations. Quarterly reserve reporting is an issuer-stated schedule, while no newer reserve report is listed. Minting remains economically unbounded under the owner-gated contracts. The prior review did not establish an arms-length prudential supervisor; supervision remains none.
